remove.why: io_uring operations (IORING_OP_OPENAT, IORING_OP_SOCKET, IORING_OP_CONNECT) are not seen by seccomp, so a ring would reopen what the filter closes. fcvm's drives use the Sync engine, so the VMM never makes one.

the fork's rule for MAP_SHARED | MAP_POPULATE is the mapping of an io_uring ring, and the VMM can make no ring without io_uring_setup. No mmap with these flags appears in the traces of this policy's audit and enforce passes on either architecture.

the VMM thread starting a block worker thread: Firecracker runs a drive on worker threads only when the drive sets num_queues, which fcvm never sends (no_drive_asks_for_worker_threads), and starts them from the VMM thread only for a drive attached to a running VM, which fcvm never does (every_drive_is_attached_before_the_guest_boots). Without it no thread of the VMM can create a thread or a process.

rule.comment: glibc's raise and abort (musl uses tkill)
glibc's pthread_kill: the vCPU kick, SIGRTMIN() + VCPU_RTSIG_OFFSET, where glibc's SIGRTMIN is 34 (musl's 35)
glibc's raise and pthread_kill pass its own pid to tgkill (musl's tkill takes none)
Rust std's metadata (fstat and stat) on a gnu target; the musl build makes fstat and newfstatat
glibc's timed wait on a process-shared futex
glibc's open on x86_64 (musl uses open, which the fork's filter lists; in the vmm class the fork's filter lists openat as well)
glibc's stat and lstat on x86_64 (musl uses stat and lstat, which the fork's filter lists)
glibc's epoll_wait on x86_64 (musl uses epoll_pwait, which the fork's filter lists)
